item.title: Friday, November 13
item.description:
Good morning. Today is Friday, November thirteenth, twenty twenty-six.

It is a sunny day in Arkadelphia with a high near fifty-eight degrees and zero percent chance of rain. A freeze warning is currently active across the region. Expect widespread frost to develop tonight after ten p.m. under mostly clear skies as the temperature drops to a low around twenty-nine degrees. Frost will remain widespread on Saturday morning before nine a.m., followed by mostly sunny skies and a high near fifty-five degrees. Sunrise was at six forty-three a.m., and sunset will be at five zero nine p.m.

Turning to the top national and world headlines.

Per NPR, Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang has stepped down following personal scandals and growing political fallout. The tech company's chief financial officer has been appointed interim chief executive officer to navigate a legal mess, ongoing supply chain concerns, and foreign export scrutiny. BBC reports that Democratic lawmakers and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have raised questions over Commerce Department oversight regarding chip exports linked to China.

In Washington politics, Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen announced he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader. Van Hollen, who serves as the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee, stated that new leadership is needed following recent midterm election results.

In international sports, United States men's national soccer team head coach Mauricio Pochettino is leaving his post. Pochettino, who led the United States to the round of sixteen at the last World Cup, has been named the new manager of Manchester United.

Meanwhile, Microsoft is working to fully restore services following a massive global tech outage. The disruption affected Outlook email, Teams videoconferencing, and Copilot software, causing delays for airlines, government offices, and businesses worldwide.

Moving over to the N-F-L and the Kansas City Chiefs.

The Kansas City Chiefs are standing by placekicker Harrison Butker despite his ongoing slump. Head coach Andy Reid and special teams coordinator Dave Toub confirmed this week that Butker will remain the starter for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons. Butker has missed seven of his nineteen field goal attempts this season, converting just over sixty-three percent of his kicks.

As Kansas City prepares for Atlanta, the Chiefs defense is focused on stopping Falcons running back Bijan Robinson, who currently leads the league in rushing yards. Robinson barely edges out Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker, who has accumulated eight hundred seventy-two yards on the year. On the Chiefs injury front, rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods missed his second straight practice Thursday with a neck injury, while starting right tackle Jaylon Moore sat out with an ankle issue. Additionally, former starting punt returner Nikko Remigio posted a goodbye message to fans after signing with the Houston Texans active roster.

Across the league, teams are evaluating their rosters following Tuesday's trade deadline as division races heat up for the second half of the season.

Next up, Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball.

The Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team continues to build momentum early in the season following a key win against Kentucky. Head coach Bill Self publicly detailed how the Jayhawks successfully neutralized Kentucky's top three-point shooter during their matchup. Highly touted freshman Tyran Stokes has also drawn attention after working on his game with former N-B-A veteran Jamal Crawford, as the coaching staff works through early-season free throw performance.

Let's check in on fantasy football.

Major injury updates are shaking up fantasy lineups for Week Ten. Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua

item.title: Thursday, November 12
item.description:
Good morning, it is Thursday, November twelfth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting in Arkadelphia, you are looking at a sunny day with a high near sixty-nine degrees, though temperatures will dip toward sixty-five this afternoon. Expect north-northwest winds around five miles per hour with gusts reaching twenty. Tonight, skies will be mostly clear with a low around thirty-three degrees, and a frost advisory is in effect. You can expect widespread frost before eight a.m. tomorrow, followed by a sunny Friday with a high near fifty-nine, with temperatures falling to around fifty-five in the afternoon. Sunrise was at six forty-two a.m. and sunset is at five oh nine p.m.

Moving to the top headlines, a tragic shooting occurred at a gym in Washington, D.C.’s Logan Circle Thursday morning. Police confirmed that one person was killed and four others were injured, and the gunman is now dead. On the international stage, U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin to discuss the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. The pair is scheduled to fly to Ireland later today for follow-up talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Meanwhile, the massive ocean liner SS United States is being sunk off the coast of Florida to be transformed into an artificial reef. In political news, Democrat Scott Colom has narrowly won the Mississippi Senate race, becoming the first Black senator in the state since eighteen seventy-four. The White House has also issued a warning to Democrats who are planning to launch investigations into the administration. Additionally, the vice president of Indonesia has resigned following questions regarding his academic credentials and eligibility, and in Italy, a second day of bomb hoax threats has forced fresh evacuations of schools across the country.

In the NFL, the Kansas City Chiefs are moving forward after acquiring wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for a pair of Day three draft selections. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes says he does not expect a long learning period for his new target and believes it is realistic for Downs to see the field quickly. On the injury front, the team’s Wednesday report showed defensive tackle Peter Woods missing practice with a neck injury, while starting right tackle Jaylon Moore also sat out with an ankle issue. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed he is sticking with veteran kicker Harrison Butker for this week’s game against the Atlanta Falcons despite a recent string of missed field goals. Defensive tackle Chris Jones has been named the AFC Defensive Player of the Week for his two-sack performance against the New York Jets. Off the field, the Chiefs have named HNTB as their official architect for stadium planning.

For Kansas men’s basketball, the Jayhawks are riding high following a dominant win over Kentucky in the Champions Classic in Chicago. The team’s deep roster and offensive firepower were on full display, with Trey Kaufman-Renn highlighted as a player making a significant difference for the squad.

Looking at fantasy football, the trade of Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs has made him a priority waiver wire pickup for managers looking for depth. With Puka Nacua dealing with an injury, Konata Mumpfield is emerging as a potential sleeper option to fill the gap. Managers should also be aware that Kewan Lacy is out for the season, and there are ongoing injury updates for players like George Pickens and A.J. Brown. For tonight’s game between the Commanders and the Giants, fantasy owners should monitor the status of running back Cam Skattebo.

item.title: Wednesday, November 11
item.description:
Good morning. Today is Wednesday, November eleventh, twenty twenty-six.

Starting with your local weather in Arkadelphia, expect sunny skies for Veterans Day with a high near seventy-nine degrees, though temperatures will dip to around seventy-five in the afternoon. Winds will come out of the west at five to ten miles per hour, bringing gusts up to twenty miles per hour, and there is only a two percent chance of rain. Tonight will be mostly clear with a low around forty-four degrees and light northwest winds. Thursday stays sunny with a high near seventy degrees, cooling to around sixty-five in the afternoon. Sunrise is at six forty-one a.m. and sunset is at five ten p.m.

Moving into national and world news, Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a major prisoner of war exchange following United States mediated talks in Abu Dhabi. According to reports from NPR and the BBC, this represents the largest humanitarian release since the conflict began in twenty twenty-two. While the negotiators discussed Europe's broader post-war security framework, the meetings concluded without a major diplomatic breakthrough.

Meanwhile, federal prosecutors have charged three alleged Iran-backed operatives over a series of plot attempts in the United Kingdom. Per BBC News, the suspects targeted nearly twenty locations, including a Royal Air Force base in Fairford that houses United States military aircraft. In related security developments, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been relocated to live on a military base due to reported threats from Iran.

On Capitol Hill, the United States House of Representatives blocked a bid to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. NPR reports that House Republicans successfully derailed the effort, though Democratic lawmakers indicated they may attempt the motion again next year. In separate leadership news, House Republicans selected a close ally of former President Donald Trump to head their minority leadership.

Over in West Africa, Senegal is preparing for a historic sporting milestone as the host of the Youth Olympic Games. Per NPR, breakdancers in the country are fine-tuning their routines ahead of the events later this month, marking the very first time an Olympic competition will take place on the African continent.

Turning to football, the Kansas City Chiefs made a major roster splash ahead of the NFL trade deadline by acquiring wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Arrowhead Pride reports that Kansas City sent fourth and fifth-round draft picks in twenty twenty-seven to secure the twenty-five-year-old receiver. To make room on the active roster, the Chiefs waived receiver Nikko Remigio and defensive end Jack Pyburn. Downs led Indianapolis with three hundred fifty-four receiving yards this season, giving quarterback Patrick Mahomes a much-needed playmaker as the team prepares to face the Atlanta Falcons.

On the defensive side of the ball, Kansas City defensive tackle Chris Jones earned his fourth career AFC Defensive Player of the Week award. According to team announcements, Jones dominated during Sunday's thirty-five to twelve victory over the New York Jets, recording two sacks, a pass breakup, and a crucial run stop. His resurgence anchored a defensive line effort that held the Jets completely out of the end zone in the second half.

In college basketball, the Kansas Jayhawks delivered a statement victory in Chicago on Tuesday night, crushing the Kentucky Wildcats eighty-nine to sixty-nine in the Champions Classic. Per the Kansas City Star, the Jayhawks put on an offensive clinic with twenty-four team assists, while guard Tyran Stokes helped fuel a commanding performance from start to finish. Kentucky struggled to find any rhythm against the Kansas defense, missing almost every shot from beyond the arc until late in the second half as Kansas co

item.title: Tuesday, November 10
item.description:
Good morning, it is Tuesday, November tenth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting with the weather in Arkadelphia, expect mostly sunny skies today with a high near seventy-four degrees, though temperatures will fall to around sixty-nine in the afternoon. Winds will be calm from the west-southwest with a six percent chance of rain. Tonight brings partly cloudy skies and a low around forty-nine. Tomorrow on Veterans Day, it will be sunny with a high near seventy-nine, dropping to around seventy-four in the afternoon, accompanied by west winds from zero to ten miles per hour and gusts up to twenty miles per hour. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise is at six forty a.m. and sunset is at five eleven p.m.

Now, the top headlines. Gasoline prices fell below four dollars a gallon for the first time in three months, though the overall cost of living remains stubbornly high, per NPR. Meanwhile, the average cost for a new vehicle in the United States hit a record high of over fifty-one thousand dollars, with some buyers extending loan terms to finance them. In international news, Russia and Ukraine held nearly four hours of United States-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, though hopes for progress are tempered by past stalemates. In North Korea, the country's spy agency says thirteen-year-old Kim Ju Ae is likely her father's heir apparent. Back in Washington, the House is set to vote on whether to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, while House Republicans prepare to vote on a successor to outgoing leader Mike Johnson following midterm losses. Additionally, the Supreme Court ruled that a federal judge lacked the authority to halt construction on the border wall.

Let's look at football, starting with the Chiefs and the NFL. The Kansas City Chiefs are preparing for their upcoming matchup against the Atlanta Falcons following a thirty-five to twelve win over the New York Jets that brings their record to six and two. Head coach Andy Reid addressed injuries on Monday, labeling quarterback Patrick Mahomes with an elbow issue, wide receiver Xavier Worthy with a hamstring issue, and right tackle Jaylon Moore with an ankle issue as day-to-day. Trade rumors continue to swirl ahead of the NFL trade deadline, with analysts viewing the Chiefs as potential suitors for additional wide receiver help. Across the league, trade deadline activity and buzz dominated headlines as teams finalized their rosters for the second half of the season.

Turning to college hoops. Kansas men's basketball is dealing with a significant backcourt blow after guard Melvin Council Junior broke the fifth metatarsal in his foot during practice on Monday. Bill Self announced that Council will undergo surgery and is expected to make a full recovery, with hopes for a return around the start of conference play. The Jayhawks are preparing for tonight's high-profile Champions Classic matchup against Kentucky in Chicago.

For fantasy football managers. If you need waiver wire help ahead of week ten, analysts are highlighting running backs like Audric Estime, Seth McGowan, and Corey Kiner as top targets. At wide receiver and other positions, streaming options and short-term fixes are widely available as managers navigate injuries and bye weeks. Avoid starting kickers like Harrison Butker and Joey Slye this week.

Over in Los Angeles. Today will be sunny with a high near eighty-eight degrees and north-northwest winds around five miles per hour. Tonight stays clear with a low around sixty-three. Tomorrow on Veterans Day, expect sunny skies and a high near eighty-six with light west-northwest winds. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise is at six twenty-one a.m. and sunset is at four fifty-two p.m.

item.title: Monday, November 9
item.description:
Good morning. Today is Monday, November ninth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting off in Arkadelphia, it is a mild and calm afternoon across the area. Expect partly sunny skies with a high near seventy-two, with temperatures gently falling to around sixty-six as the afternoon winds down. Winds will stay light and calm. Tonight brings mostly cloudy conditions with a low dropping to around forty-two, and virtually no chance of rain. Tomorrow looks bright and mostly sunny, reaching a high near seventy-five. Sunrise was at six thirty-nine a.m., sunset is at five twelve p.m., and there are no active weather alerts.

Turning to top headlines from around the nation and across the globe.

In London, British comedian and actor Russell Brand has been sentenced to ten and a half years in prison following his conviction on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The case was brought forward by six women, capping a dramatic legal downfall for the former Hollywood star who had reinvented himself in recent years as an online political commentator.

On Capitol Hill, Republican Representative Thomas Massie has officially introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Massie is forcing a vote over the launch and continuation of military operations in Iran without congressional authorization, using the maneuver to pressure Donald Trump to remove Hegseth before incoming Democrats take control of the House.

Meanwhile, Donald Trump took to Truth Social on Monday to question the integrity of last week's midterm elections, casting doubt on the results without evidence after previously accepting the Republican losses. At the same time, Trump announced the appointment of Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff, signaling an aggressive posture toward congressional opposition.

Overseas, European authorities are pointing fingers at Tehran after a major cyber incident. France and the United States suspect Iran orchestrated a cyberattack against European grocery chains, hacking refrigeration systems in hundreds of supermarkets and spoiling tons of chilled and frozen food.

Over in the NFL, the Kansas City Chiefs got back into the win column and received encouraging news on their franchise quarterback.

Kansas City snapped a two-game skid on Sunday with a thirty-five to twelve victory over the New York Jets at Arrowhead Stadium, improving to six and two. Running back Kenneth Walker drove the offense with one hundred forty-three yards from scrimmage, while Chris Jones and George Karlaftis led a resurgent pass rush that battered the Jets. The afternoon also featured a major milestone, as Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce officially set the NFL record for the most receiving yards by a quarterback and tight end duo, surpassing nine thousand three hundred sixty career yards.

The biggest scare came when Mahomes took a hard hit to his elbow, but head coach Andy Reid delivered an optimistic update Monday, describing the quarterback as day-to-day and calling the evaluation more positive than negative. Looking ahead, the Chiefs are three and a half point road favorites against the Atlanta Falcons in Week ten. With the league trade deadline arriving Tuesday at three p.m. Arrowhead time, Reid noted general manager Brett Veach is keeping his eyes open, with speculation mounting that Kansas City could pursue wide receiver help. Elsewhere in the AFC, Jacksonville routed Baltimore thirty-three to ten, Cincinnati topped Atlanta thirty-four to seventeen in Madrid, and the conference-leading Buffalo Bills face Minnesota tonight.

On the college hardwood, the Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team is preparing for an early-season rivalry clash against Kentucky.

item.title: Sunday, November 8
item.description:
Good morning. Today is Sunday, November eighth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting off in Arkadelphia, expect partly sunny skies today with an afternoon high near sixty-nine degrees, though temperatures will ease down to around sixty-five as the afternoon wears on. Winds will remain nearly calm, and the rain chance sits at zero percent. Tonight will stay partly cloudy and chilly, with the overnight low dropping down to around thirty-five degrees. Sunrise was at six thirty-eight this morning, and sunset will be at five twelve p.m., with no active weather watches or warnings across the area.

Turning to the top headlines from around the world. In Israel, President Isaac Herzog has officially tapped opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government, bypassing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The decision follows last week's election where neither Netanyahu's bloc nor his rivals secured a clear majority, but major parties rallied behind Eisenkot. The former military chief now has twenty-eight days to build a coalition that can control at least sixty-one seats in the one hundred twenty seat parliament.

In Poland, authorities say a gunman who killed six people in Krakow's historic main market square on Saturday held ultranationalistic views. The attacker drove into the tourist hub and opened fire on bystanders before being wounded and captured during a gunfight with police. Investigators later discovered three additional bodies at the suspect's residence, bringing the total death toll tied to the suspect to nine.

In South America, ousted Paraguayan President Santiago Peña has appeared before prosecutors after being removed from office and placed under house arrest on Friday. The Paraguayan Senate voted to impeach Peña following the sudden collapse of a state-affiliated bank, an economic crisis that left millions of citizens unable to access their savings.

Back in Washington, political shockwaves from the midterm elections continue to ripple through the capital. President Donald Trump has offered the post of White House press secretary to UFC boss Dana White, who confirmed he plans to meet with the president on Monday to discuss the role. Meanwhile, exit polling reveals that voters under thirty broke decisively for Democrats, reversing prior Republican gains with younger voters and powering significant Democratic victories nationwide.

In NFL action, the Kansas City Chiefs return home to Arrowhead Stadium this afternoon to host the New York Jets in a crucial Week Nine contest. Kansas City is desperate to right the ship after back-to-back defeats, having fallen twenty to three against Seattle before dropping a twenty-eight to twenty-four heartbreaker to Denver last week. Patrick Mahomes and the offense showed signs of life against the Broncos with three hundred ninety-nine total yards, including a seventy-three-yard touchdown run from rookie Emmett Johnson. Ahead of kickoff, tight end Noah Gray expressed strong confidence in the offensive unit, while the Chiefs shored up their defensive front by elevating tackle Marcus Harris from the practice squad. Injury reports are also keeping fans on edge as the team monitors the game-day availability of tight end Travis Kelce, wide receiver Rashee Rice, and defensive back Mansoor Delane.

Across the wider league, coaching hot seats are becoming a major talking point as the season hits its midpoint. Per Arrowhead Pride, fan confidence across several franchises has tumbled, with Tampa Bay's Todd Bowles, Green Bay's Matt LaFleur, and the Chargers' Jim Harbaugh facing heightened pressure to turn their seasons around before the playoff race slips away.

item.title: Saturday, November 7
item.description:
Good morning. Today is Saturday, November seventh, twenty twenty-six.

Starting in Arkadelphia, we have partly sunny skies ahead today with a high near sixty-five degrees and calm winds out of the northeast. Rain chances sit at zero percent through both the day and night. Tonight turns partly cloudy as temperatures dip to a low around thirty-six degrees. The sun rose at six thirty-seven this morning and will set at five thirteen this evening.

Turning to the top headlines around the world. President Donald Trump has chosen Stephen Miller to take over as his chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. The staff shakeup follows sweeping Republican losses in Tuesday's midterm elections and sets up an aggressive posture heading into clashes with the new Democratic Congress. Trump confirmed on sixty minutes that personnel changes were imminent, hours before making the announcement. Down in South America, Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest after a sudden banking collapse left millions of citizens unable to access their savings. Pope Leo has begun a twelve-day, three-country tour of South America just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer. The trip takes him through Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, with the Vatican reporting the pontiff is in good health for his first journey to the region since the operation. In the United States, the incoming class of senators will include several historic firsts, featuring the first Native American woman elected to the chamber, the first Muslim senator, and the chamber's first Paralympian. Meanwhile, counting drags on in Mississippi's razor-thin Senate race between Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom, spotlighting the state's slow and decentralized counting process.

Moving to football, the Kansas City Chiefs return home to Arrowhead Stadium tomorrow to take on the two and six New York Jets. The Chiefs sit at five and two and are trying to snap a frustrating two-game losing streak. Last week, Kansas City controlled most of the game against Denver before a fourth-quarter collapse handed the Broncos a twenty-eight to twenty-four win. Head coach Andy Reid faces second-year Jets coach Aaron Glenn, with Kansas City entering as nine and a half point favorites. The injury report brings trouble on defense. Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods is ruled out with a neck injury after missing practice all week, and rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane is also out. Off the field, wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy following numerous lawsuits tied to his twenty twenty-four car crash. For New York, running back Breece Hall is set to return to action, giving the Jets a much-needed boost after dropping three straight games.

On the college hardwood, the Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team rolled to a blowout victory over Middle Tennessee State at Allen Fieldhouse. Kansas entered the night favored by twenty-seven and a half points and put the game away early. Despite the lopsided win, head coach Bill Self noted postgame that he still has real concerns about his squad, pointing specifically to early-season struggles at the free-throw line. Roster adjustments are also in motion, with forward Trey Kaufman-Renn looking to earn a starting role after opening the year coming off the bench. The Jayhawks now turn their attention toward a heavyweight showdown against Kentucky.

Looking at fantasy football heading into Sunday's Week Nine slate, injuries are forcing tough lineup decisions. Running back Cam Skattebo is listed as doubtful, meaning fantasy managers must line up a replacement immediately. On the positive side, Travis Kelce is on track to play for Kansas City against the Jets, keeping him locked into starting tight end slots.
